notes: Scenario estimates, not deployed-scale measurements or provider quotes. USD before tax; US East geography: DigitalOcean NYC1 and Pinecone AWS us-east-1. Prices/rate assumptions frozen for reproducibility; verify provider calculator before purchasing.
One self-hosted node, one replica, no availability SLA; vendor handles managed replication. Reliability is not equivalent.

1000 serial queries/month, one namespace, k=3, no large fetch/export workload; 1% records updated monthly. Response egress stays below the stated plan allowances. No embedding, generator, judge, engineering labor, tax or migration costs in this store-only comparison.

Pinecone namespace GB uses decimal 1e9 bytes. RU/query=max(0.25,namespace_GB). Updates modeled conservatively as old+new record bytes in decimal KB; small-request minimum overhead is omitted assuming batches. Initial loading shown separately, not silently amortized into recurring totals.

At 100K the managed free tier can be cheaper than a VM. Table includes the cheapest eligible Starter/Builder/Standard scenario alongside Standard-only cost. Builder/Starter quota assumptions are suitable only for this light workload and should be checked before migration.

SQLite uses exact cosine scans, not an ANN index. At 10M the vector file exceeds RAM and latency can be unacceptable despite fitting on disk. Small-corpus latency must NOT be extrapolated to these scales. Move to pgvector/Qdrant ANN or managed infrastructure when latency or operations require it.
